items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Alice Whitman was the first woman tap dancer that I had ever seen and she was a great one.

ctx.x: Another movie and vaudeville house opened on Central Avenue between 4th and 5th Streets and it was there that I saw Mamie Smith, Ma Rainey and Bessie Smith, the most famous of all the women blues singers. I also worked for one week at this show place. There was a part in the show about a man, his wife and their many children coming from the South to visit some relatives in the North. There must have been about 10 of us and all living in Hathaway Street. We did two shows a day and were very proud that we were…

The Whitman Sisters show was another one that came very often to Cincinnati. I do not remember anything interesting concerning the musical background of the show but Alice Whitman was the first woman tap dancer that I had ever seen and she was a great one.

Negro people could go to the shows up_town but they had to sit in the second balcony which was known as the peanut gallery. There was no segregation in the peanut gallery because white people who didn't have enough to sit on the first floor or the first balcony, sat next to the negros and conversed with them. I used to go quite often to the Keith Theatre on Walnut Street which was in the shopping centre of the city.
